chunks: From him, from Ishaq, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The land is leased for wheat, or for dates, or for barley, or for four qirats of silk, or for four qirats of silk cocoons.

key_terms.الْأَرْبِعَاءِ: Four qirats (a unit of weight, referring to silk)
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: Land (specifically agricultural land in this context)

ai.seo_question: What commodities can be used to pay rent for leasing agricultural land according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the validity of *ijar al-ard* (land leasing) by specifying permissible commodities—wheat, dates, barley, silk, and cocoons—as rent, reflecting the agricultural economy of early Shia communities. It serves as a foundational text for jurists distinguishing valid lease contracts from invalid ones, emphasizing that the rent must be a known, tangible asset rather than an uncertain future yield. This ruling supports the broader Shia legal principle of allowing flexible economic arrangements in agriculture while maintaining clarity in contractual obligations.
